scenario.summary: Amatera is a C++ infostealer distributed via 'ClickFix' social engineering, SEO poisoning, and malicious ads targeting developers. Once executed, it establishes persistence through scheduled tasks and exfiltrates browser credentials, session tokens, and sensitive files from local systems and cloud storage services like SharePoint.

meta.rationale: The campaign specifically targets developers and users of AI tools. Focus first on workstations with JetBrains, Claude, or Snowflake client software. Use a 14-day lookback to capture both the initial social engineering (ClickFix) and subsequent persistence mechanisms.
meta.hypothesis: An intruder has used social engineering to trick a user into executing PowerShell commands from the Run dialog, leading to the installation of the Amatera infostealer and persistent scheduled tasks.

blind_spots.risk: The hunt relies on the process parent-child relationship (explorer -> powershell) and command line content, which can be bypassed if the user runs the command through other means.

blind_spots.remediation: Explore EDR capability for monitoring clipboard-to-command-line transfers.

hunt.name: Amatera Infostealer Initial Access and Persistence
hunt.description: Amatera is a professionalized infostealer that frequently uses ClickFix techniques, where victims are social-engineered into pasting malicious commands directly into Windows system utilities. This hunt identifies the initial user-driven execution, corroborates it with known network infrastructure, and then tracks follow-on persistence and defense evasion through PowerShell history tampering.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, package_name, package_version FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE (instr(',' || '{{dev_tool_patterns}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(package_name) || ',') > 0) GROUP BY device_hostname, package_name, package_version
config.description: Identify hosts running tools mentioned in the Amatera campaign to prioritize the hunt on developer workstations.
config.expected_signal: A list of hosts frequently using AI or development tools. Silence means no such software was found, not that the hosts are safe.

primitive_config.label: Scope to developer workstations

primitive_config.expected: A list of hosts frequently using AI or development tools. Silence means no such software was found, not that the hosts are safe.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_cmd_line, parent_process_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(parent_process_name) LIKE '%\explorer.exe') AND (LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\powershell.exe' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\rundll32.exe') AND (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%-enc%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%invoke-webrequest%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%iwr%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Find PowerShell or Rundll32 processes launched directly from explorer.exe, which is the hallmark of the ClickFix social engineering vector.
config.expected_signal: PowerShell commands with obfuscated or download-related flags launched by explorer.exe. This typically represents a user pasting a command from the browser.

primitive_config.label: PowerShell execution from Run dialog

config.objective: Determine if any host shows evidence of a user-driven infection via pasted commands corroborated by network activity.
config.description: Analyze whether the observed process execution and DNS traffic indicate a successful user-initiated infection.
config.expected_signal: A per-host verdict identifying whether the execution was likely malicious.
config.success_criteria: A verdict for each host with supporting row citations.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, job_name, job_cmd_line, job_user_name, time FROM hb_scheduled_job WHERE activity_id IN (1, 2) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0)
config.description: Amatera is known to create unusual scheduled tasks for persistence. This query finds jobs created or updated during the lookback period.
config.expected_signal: Creation of non-standard tasks, particularly those running PowerShell or binaries from user-writable paths.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, file_path, process_name, activity_name, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY file_path) as global_frequency, time FROM hb_file_activity WHERE LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\microsoft\windows\powershell\powershell\consolehost_history.txt' AND activity_id IN (3, 4) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0)
config.description: The report suggests attackers clear PowerShell history to hide the pasted commands. This query finds deletions of the ConsoleHost_history.txt file.
config.expected_signal: Deletions or suspicious updates to the PowerShell history file. This is rare in standard administrative workflows.

config.description: Final analyst confirmation and follow-on remediation steps.
